chunks: From him, from his father, from the one who mentioned it to whom it reached, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
He said: 'The worst servant is a servant for whom there is greed driving him, and the worst servant is a servant for whom there is a desire disgracing him.'

key_terms.تُذِلُّهُ: Disgracing or humiliating him, indicating the degrading effect of desire.
key_terms.رَغْبَةٌ: Desire or longing, here specified as that which causes humiliation.
key_terms.طَمَعٌ: Greed or avarice, a driving force that leads one astray.
key_terms.يَقُودُهُ: Driving him or leading him, indicating the active control of greed.

ai.seo_question: What makes a servant 'worst' in the eyes of Imam al-Baqir according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies greed (*tam'*) and desire (*raghbah*) as the two primary internal forces that degrade the status of a servant of God. This teaching aligns with the Shia ethical tradition of *adab al-nafs* (discipline of the self), where unchecked appetites are seen not merely as sins but as structural impediments to spiritual dignity and divine proximity. The hadith serves as a diagnostic tool for believers to distinguish between the leading nature of greed and the humiliating nature of base desires.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from the one who mentioned it to whom it reached, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>:
‘The worst servant is a servant for whom there is greed driving him, and so also the is a servant for whom there is a desire disgracing him’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from those whom he has mentioned in his book from abu Ja’far (a.s.)
who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘The worst servant is the servant who has a greed that dominates him and so also is a servant whose desires humiliate him.’”
